evidence.field: 形義通解；字形與構件分析
evidence.text: The entry analyzes the bronze form of 送 as 辵 (walking) plus phonetic 灷. It describes the bronze 灷 as 廾 plus 丨 with decorative dots and says that shape changes in small-seal writing; it also says 灷 is the phonetic in 送、媵、賸. This is the entry’s account, not a directly dated palaeographic demonstration. Separately, Shuowen’s transmitted analysis reads “送，遣也。从辵，㑞省。𨕼，籀文不省.”
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「送」

evidence.source: 《說文解字》 record reproduced in 漢語多功能字庫 (CUHK)
evidence.text: The reproduced entry glosses 送 as 遣 and analyzes it as 从辵、㑞省, with 𨕼 as the unsimplified 籀文 form. This is a historical lexicographic analysis; it does not independently establish that the bronze graph’s phonetic component was 㑞.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「送」

evidence.source: 復旦大學出土文獻與古文字研究中心
evidence.field: 《雲漢：楚簡一類寫作“〖辵臼丨豕〗”形的“送”字補說》；楚簡釋形與形體討論
evidence.text: The author identifies several Chu-slip graphs as 送 because their contexts correspond to received Shijing text, and discusses multiple graph shapes. The paper proposes paths involving hands, an 八-like stroke, 又, and forms liable to be read as 豕; it also says one discussed shape cannot simply be placed into a linear evolution sequence on shape alone. This complicates a single bronze-to-seal narrative; the article was published 2023-12-05.
evidence.title: 雲漢：楚簡一類寫作“〖辵臼丨豕〗”形的“送”字補說

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 研訂瀏覽；送 and 𨕩 entries
evidence.text: The dictionary reproduces the Shuowen definition and says its 籀文 form 𨕩 is written with 辵 and a fuller left-side form; in the standard form, 辵 is positionalized as 辶. Its readings section records Mandarin sòng. This supports the Shuowen form contrast and positional shape description, not a chronology for the word’s senses.
evidence.title: [A04127] 送 - Ministry of Education 《Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants》2024

evidence.text: The entry records the Guangyun fanqie 蘇弄 and the Shuowen gloss 遣也. These medieval and Han-dynasty lexicographic records attest those readings/glosses in their respective sources; gloss order does not date the onset of semantic extensions.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「送」

evidence.source: Chinese Text Project, Book of Poetry
evidence.text: The received poem includes 送我乎淇之上矣; its supplied English translation interprets this context as accompanying someone to the Qi river. This is evidence for an early received-text use in an accompanying/sending context, but neither the poem’s precise composition date nor a transition from this use to later senses is established here. Direct opening of this page returned 403; its search result was inspected.
evidence.title: 詩經 : 國風 : 鄘風 : 桑中 - 中國哲學書電子化計劃

evidence.field: 方壺 inscription transcription and description
evidence.text: The page identifies the Zhongshan king vessel inscriptions as Warring States and dates the king’s 14th year to approximately 314 BCE; its transcription of the Fanghu includes “惟朕皇祖…”. The CUHK entry separately reports a graph in the round-pot inscription read as 朕, rather than the verb 送. That reading concerns a graph in a specific inscription and does not establish general whole-graph borrowing or the pronunciation/name of an object depicted by the graph.
evidence.title: 中山王器銘文

evidence.text: The 送 entry assigns 灷 a phonetic role, but provides no historical pronunciation comparison for 灷 and 送. The local Unihan kMandarin rows supplied for 灷 and 送 are zhuàn and sòng respectively (sources/unihan/Unihan_Readings.txt; rows 灷 and 送); they are current metadata and do not establish an ancient sound relation. The local Baxter–Sagart table row supplied for 送 is MC suwngH, OC *[s]ˤoŋ-s (sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv; row 送); there is no supplied 灷 row for comparison. The official Unicode pages for both code points could not be verified in this session.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「送」

evidence.text: The official character-specific records were attempted for 送 (U+9001) and 灷 (U+7077), but the 送 request timed out and the 灷 URL was not accessible through the research tool. search_audit.outcome: Search identified unrelated character files with ancient-script licenses, but not a 送 glyph asset. No candidate direct image URL was proposed.

gaps: The exact Commons 送 seal-file description page was not openable, so there is no verified direct original image URL; no usable direct glyph image is proposed. Sinica's 送 evolution page says All Rights Reserved; it is evidence only, not an image source. Xiaoxuetang produced no character-specific 送 record in this search.

The CUHK component assignment 灷 is not accompanied by a historical reconstruction for 灷 comparable to the local Baxter–Sagart reconstruction for 送. The proposed sound role is the dictionary's explicit analysis, but an independently demonstrated sound correspondence cannot be reported. Local rows: sources/unihan/Unihan_Readings.txt kMandarin 灷=zhuàn and 送=sòng; sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv row 送 MC suwngH, OC *[s]ˤoŋ-s. Official Unicode records failed to load, so they cannot serve as click-through evidence.

The Fudan paper discusses Chu-slip forms and possible graphic corruption/merger pathways, including debated analysis of shapes read as 豕. It cautions against a simple form sequence for at least one graph. A fuller palaeographic resolution is not established by the opened paper excerpt.

The received Shijing use supports an accompanying/sending context, but its composition date and a chronological pathway to dispatch, give, deliver, or escort remain unestablished. Dictionary gloss ordering is not chronology.

The bronze form reported as 朕 is a distinct reading in a specific Zhongshan inscription, dated by the vessel context to around 314 BCE; this does not prove a general loan history for the graph. The depicted-object/phonetic borrowing hypothesis is unsupported and no object name or pronunciation can be recovered from the inspected evidence.
No permission terms for extracting or mirroring recurring dictionary text were verified; no local extract is recommended.

limitations.text: No image candidate met the requirement for a verified exact source page and directly copied image URL: Commons search exposed a CC0 Shuowen seal-file result but exact description-page opening failed; Sinica's character-specific evolution page explicitly states All Rights Reserved; Xiaoxuetang's opened general interface did not return a character-specific 送 image. Thus no glyph is proposed.
